title: KYC and CDD Standards
body:
KYC and CDD Standards
Owner: Compliance (author: Daniel Sanchez, AML Investigator)
Last updated: 2026-08-18
Approved by: Marcus Bell, Chief Compliance Officer

Purpose
This standard sets out the minimum Know Your Customer (KYC) and Customer Due Diligence (CDD) requirements for every client onboarded by Halcyon Ridge Capital, across Wealth Management, Lending, Trading and M&A Advisory. It applies to all front-office staff who open or sponsor a relationship and to the Compliance and Operations staff who screen and approve them.

Scope and Systems
All onboarding is run through KYCPipeline, our client onboarding KYC/CDD screening pipeline. KYCPipeline pulls client records from ClientHub, collects supporting documents from DocVault, and calls SanctionsScreen for OFAC and sanctions list screening. No account, loan facility or trading line may be activated until KYCPipeline shows an approved status. LoanOrigination also depends on KYCPipeline, so Lending cannot move a file to credit decisioning with an open KYC item.

Ownership Transition
KYCPipeline is currently operated by Operations under Ravi Patel. Ownership transfers to Compliance on 2026-10-06. Until that date, pipeline defects and configuration changes go to Operations. From 2026-10-06, they go to Compliance, with Jenna Cho as engineering lead. Policy decisions on screening rules have always been Compliance's, and that does not change.

Standard Due Diligence
For every client the relationship owner must collect and the KYC Specialist must verify:
- Legal identity and a government-issued identification document, or formation documents for entities
- Residential or registered business address
- Nature and purpose of the relationship and the expected activity
- Source of funds, and source of wealth for wealth and lending clients
- Beneficial owners at or above 25 percent ownership, and any person with control, for entity clients
- Politically exposed person status, checked at onboarding and at each periodic review

Documents are stored only in DocVault. Do not keep copies in email, shared drives or chat. Do not paste client identifiers into Slack channels, including #kyc-pipeline.

Enhanced Due Diligence
Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is required where any of the following applies:
- Politically exposed persons and their close associates
- Clients with a nexus to a high-risk jurisdiction as listed in the current Compliance country matrix
- Complex ownership structures, including trusts and offshore holding companies
- Digital asset activity, pending the final output of the #crypto-policy working group
- Adverse media or a screening hit that cannot be cleared at first review

EDD cases need additional source of wealth corroboration, senior management sign-off from the relevant business head, and approval by Compliance before activation. Nadia Petrov's AML team reviews all EDD files.

Sanctions Screening
SanctionsScreen runs automatically at onboarding and on every list update. Screening covers the client, beneficial owners, controllers and authorized signatories. Potential matches are never cleared by the relationship owner. A KYC Specialist reviews each alert, documents the rationale, and escalates unresolved matches to the AML team the same business day. A confirmed match is blocked immediately and reported to the CCO.

Risk Rating and Periodic Review
Each client is rated low, medium or high at onboarding. Review cycles are:
- High risk: every 12 months
- Medium risk: every 24 months
- Low risk: every 36 months

A trigger event, such as a change in ownership, unusual activity flagged by AMLMonitor, or a SAR filing, prompts an off-cycle review regardless of schedule.

Roles and Responsibilities
Relationship owners in Wealth, Lending and M&A are accountable for complete, accurate onboarding information. KYC Specialists, including John Smith and Luis Bowen, verify documents and work screening alerts. The AML team handles EDD and escalations. Compliance Engineering maintains the pipeline rules. Operations supports the platform until the transition date.

Service Levels
A complete standard-risk file should be decided within three business days of the last document being received. EDD files have no fixed turnaround, and business pressure is not a reason to shorten them. Incomplete files are returned to the relationship owner with a list of missing items.

Record Retention
KYC records are kept for at least five years after the relationship ends, or longer where required by regulation or a legal hold. Retention is managed through DocVault.

Exceptions and Questions
Exceptions to this standard need written approval from the CCO. Questions can be posted in #compliance or sent directly to Daniel Sanchez.
